?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:74732
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 14228 of 2021

Applicant :- Gyanendra Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Hemant Kumar Mishra,Arti Ganguly Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J. 
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 229 of 2021, under Sections 420/409/504/506/120B IPC,
Police Station Gomti Nagar, District Lucknow.

It has been contended by learned counsel for the applicant that vide order dated 13th of December,
2021, the applicant was granted conditional bail.
The order dated 13th of December, 2021 is reproduced hereunder:
"Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

The Counsel for the applicant offers to pay an amount of Rs.6,26,000/- which was agreed to be paid in between the informant and the applicant and for which the cheque no.015955 was issued which stood dishonored on 30.11.2020.
Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the applicant is ready to pay the amount which was agreed between the applicant and the informant coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 07.08.2021, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on interim bail.

Let the applicant Gyanendra Singh be released on interim bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.229 of 2021, under Sections 420, 409, 504, 506, 120B IPC, Police Station Gomtinagar, District Lucknow on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.10,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(1) The applicant shall pay the agreed amount within 30 days from the date of release to the informant.

In case, the applicant does not pay the amount as undertaken and recorded above, the applicant shall surrender before the trial court on the 30th day of the date of release and if the applicant is in custody in other cases also, the date of payment of 30 days shall start from the date of actual release from the custody.
(2) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence, if the witnesses are present in Court.

In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;
(3) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;

(4). In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(5) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
The question of final bail shall be considered after complying the abovesaid undertakings.
List this case on 15.03.2022 for consideration of final bail."

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant added that the condition was imposed that within the period of 30 days, the applicant shall pay the agreed amount and in compliance thereof the amount Rs.6,26,000/- has been paid through RTGS to the complainant, namely, Jawahar Yadav on 11th of April, 2022 and a copy of the RTGS statement has also been appended alongwith the affidavit dated 12.04.2022.
She further submits that the applicant is cooperating with the trial proceedings and he undertakes that he will never jump the bail and will always cooperate the trial proceeding.

She added that there are as many as 9 cases criminal history of the applicant which has been explained and those are in the nature of civil liability and some cases relate to money transaction and in almost all the cases, the money has been returned back.
Thus, she submits that the applicant may be granted regular bail.

Per contra, learned AGA appearing for the State has opposed the aforesaid contentions on merits but he could not dispute the fact regarding payment of agreed amount Rs.6,26,000/-, as is transcribed in the affidavit dated 12.04.2022 filed by the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the record, it transpires that the conditional bail was granted to the applicant vide order dated 13.12.2021 and the fact remains that the condition has successfully been complied with by the applicant which is evident from the affidavit dated 12.04.2022.

As per instruction of learned counsel for the State, there is no complaint with respect to non-cooperation of the present applicant regarding trial of Case Crime No. 229 of 2021; the criminal history of the applicant has been explained and it has been undertaken by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant will cooperate in the trial proceedings.

Considering all over the facts, submissions of learned counsels for the parties, nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction, nature of supporting evidence, prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformative theory of punishment and considering larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case of bail.

If the bail bonds and sureties have already been furnished by the applicant to the court concerned,
no further bail bonds and sureties are required.
He shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

sentences.text: (3) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.; and (4) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
It is clarified that the observations made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the merits of the case.
